atoms.name: Layers and PDUs
atoms.one_line: Application message, transport segment, network packet, data link frame, physical bits. Each layer owns one scope.

atoms.name: Layer visits per path
atoms.one_line: k links give k+1 network-layer visits and 2k data-link visits. Routers rebuild the frame, not the packet.

atoms.name: Circuit, packet and virtual circuit
atoms.one_line: Circuit reserves a path and rate (setup, TDM/FDM slots). Packet switching shares links. Virtual circuit sets a fixed route with a short label.

atoms.name: The four delays
atoms.one_line: Transmission L/R, propagation d/s, processing, queuing. First two are formulas; queuing depends on traffic.

atoms.name: Store-and-forward and pipelining
atoms.one_line: A router receives a whole packet before sending it on: one packet costs k Tt. N equal packets finish at (N+k-1)Tt plus k Tp; headers trade against pipelining.

atoms.name: Bottleneck and bandwidth-delay product
atoms.one_line: Streaming rate is the minimum link rate. Bits in flight on a link are R times Tp.

atoms.name: Queuing and traffic intensity
atoms.one_line: Intensity La/R; queue delay climbs as it nears 1 and is unbounded at 1 or more.

atoms.name: Switch port counting
atoms.one_line: n switches in a tree use 2(n-1) ports to interconnect; the rest serve hosts.

patterns.name: Stop-and-wait and window delay problems (see net.datalink)
